$comment: Corrections applied on top of the reference gir files. 'skip' removes symbols from generation - a callable by c:identifier, a type by its qualified gir name, a property by its GObject spelling -, 'forceOpaque' keeps a record behind a pointer instead of copying it by value, 'rename' overrides the derived C# name, 'annotationOverrides' patches wrong or missing transfer/nullable/array annotations and states the facts about a C function that no gir annotation carries - the 'direction' of a pointer to a plain structure, to a GValue, to a scalar, to an enumeration or to a record the function works on in place, and the 'fixedArraySize' of a caller allocated out array and the 'scope' of a callback parameter the library keeps longer than the gir says; a signal argument is addressed by the GObject spelling of its signal, 'GES.Project::error-loading-asset#error', where only 'nullable' and 'borrow' are read - the second hands the handler a borrowed wrapper of a mini object or boxed argument, see '$comment-borrow-signal-arguments'; on the bare identifier of a callable it may also state 'obsolete', the message of an [Obsolete] attribute the emitted member carries; 'arrayOverrides' corrects the length, the fixed size, the zero termination or the element type of an <array> the gir already spells, 'returnTypeOverrides' narrows a returned handle onto the type that declares the member.
$comment-skip-static-str: The *_static_str family stores the string the caller passes by pointer and never copies it, so the string has to outlive every use of the object it was stored in. The generated marshalling hands native code a stack or heap buffer that is released when the call returns, which leaves the library holding a dangling pointer for every string that does not fit the short string optimisation. The gir carries no annotation that says a string must be static, so there is nothing for the planner to key on and the symbols are listed here. Binding them needs hand written glue that hands over an interned copy. The three *_value_static_str entries are the same family for the field name string of a value write: gstidstr-private.h:130-132 inline-copies a name of at most 15 bytes and aliases the caller's pointer beyond that, a silent, length dependent dangling hazard. gst_structure_take_value_static_str would also be rejected as a consuming take_value; it is listed here with the static-str rationale so that a future take-value emission cannot bind it either.
$comment-skip-identity: gst_buffer_remove_meta is hand bound as Gst.Buffer.RemoveMeta. The identity fault this entry was first written for is gone - '$comment-force-opaque-meta' keeps GstMeta behind a pointer, so the call is handed the address the buffer handed out - and what kept it out afterwards was the other end: removing a metadata item frees it synchronously (gstbuffer.c:gst_buffer_remove_meta unlinks, calls info->free_func and g_frees the item before it returns), and the wrapper the caller passed in is a bare pointer holder that nothing invalidates. That is what the hand written member adds and no emission shape expresses: it zeroes the wrapper's handle when, and only when, the call answers TRUE, because every FALSE path (not writable, GST_META_FLAG_LOCKED, a meta of another buffer) leaves the item alive. Gst.Buffer.ForeachMeta applies the same convention to the item a callback asks to remove.
$comment-skip-annotations: These five functions carry annotations that do not describe what the C function does, and following them produces wrong lengths or wrong ownership: gst_adapter_map returns a pointer whose length is the size argument rather than an annotated array, gst_adapter_take returns freshly allocated memory of the size argument, gst_type_find_peek returns a borrowed pointer of the size argument, and gst_audio_ring_buffer_commit both reads and writes its sample count while its data pointer carries no length at all. An annotation override cannot add a missing array length, so they are skipped.
$comment-skip-sample-count: gst_audio_ring_buffer_read is the same family as gst_audio_ring_buffer_commit above, with the twist that its annotation is present and reads as correct. Its data array is annotated with the len parameter as its length, but len counts samples while the array counts bytes, and the C function writes bytes_per_frame bytes for each sample it is asked for. The emitted call took the byte length of the span for the sample count, so every format wider than one byte per frame - which is every format an application actually uses, S16LE stereo being four - had the library write bytes_per_frame times past the end of the caller's memory. No annotation states the unit of a length, so there is nothing for the planner to key on. The call is bound in Gst.Audio.AudioRingBuffer.Read instead, with the same signature, where the span is measured in samples before it is handed over.
$comment-skip-consumed: gst_meta_info_register consumes the GstMetaInfo it is given and returns the registered one. The wrapper of an opaque record owns nothing and is never disposed, so nothing is freed twice, but the instance the caller still holds points at released memory the moment the call returns. That is also why a generated member would be unreachable surface: the block it consumes can only come from gst_meta_info_new, which no managed code can call. Both halves are hand bound now, inside Gst.Meta.Register in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/MetaAuthor.cs, which is the only place the pair is ever used and the only window in which the function fields of a block are writable; see $comment-hand-bound-meta-authorship.
$comment-skip-superseded: gst_adapter_unmap releases what gst_adapter_map handed out, and gst_adapter_map is skipped just above. Emitting the release on its own leaves a public Unmap() with no Map() to pair it with, which unmaps a mapping the caller never took and releases a second time the one that the hand written scope holds. The mapping surface of an adapter is Gst.Base.Adapter.Map and the scope it returns, so this entry point is bound there and nowhere else.
$comment-skip-sync-handler: gst_bus_set_sync_handler installs a callback whose return value decides who owns the message: GST_BUS_DROP makes the handler responsible for unreffing it, every other reply leaves that to gst_bus_post. No annotation of the gir states a transfer that a return value turns on, so the generated marshalling cannot express it, and the emitted call had two faults because of it. It refused a null handler, which made the documented clear form unreachable and left a consumer unable to take the handler off at teardown; and its trampoline handed the managed handler a borrowed wrapper, so a handler that answered Drop leaked the reference of the poster with no way of consuming it from managed code. Both are fixed in Gst.Bus.SetSyncHandler and Gst.Bus.ClearSyncHandler, whose hand written trampoline drops that reference itself when the handler answers Drop. The delegate is hand written next to the install so that its documentation can state the contract the binding actually implements. Skipping the call no longer retires the generated GstBusSyncHandler on its own, because a hand bound consumer keeps its callback type generated; the type entry on the skip list is what does, see $comment-skip-hand-written-callback-types.
$comment-skip-deinit: ges_deinit releases everything ges_init built, and the editing services are unusable until another ges_init. The binding runs ges_init from GstGES.Initialize, behind a latch that says it has run, and nothing in the library tells that latch when the resources are gone: a caller who takes the shut down of the process into their own hands leaves the entry point of the module reporting an initialised GES that no longer exists, and no call can bring it back. This is the shape gst_adapter_unmap has, a release with no acquisition of its own to pair with, and the same answer. Deinitialising GES is what ending the process does, which the documentation of the C function says as well.
$comment-skip-unpaired: gst_adapter_unmap releases a mapping this binding has no way of taking: gst_adapter_map is hand bound behind Gst.Base.Adapter.Map, whose scope performs the release, so every call Unmap() could receive would unmap a mapping the caller never took. The audio and video counterparts used to be listed here for the same reason and are now owned by their own scopes, see $comment-skip-scope-owned.
$comment-skip-credentials: gst_rtsp_auth_credentials_free frees a NULL terminated array of GstRTSPAuthCredential, and the gir spells its parameter as a bare 'GstRTSPAuthCredential**' with no array element on it. The planner reads that as one handle, so the emitted call hands the library the address of a single credential and the loop inside the C function walks past it and frees whatever the words that follow happen to point at. No caller could get it right either: the only producer of such an array is gst_rtsp_message_parse_auth_credentials, whose out array is unannotated in the same way and which is skipped for it, so what a caller can hold is one GstRTSPAuthCredential. That one is a boxed wrapper which frees its own copy when it is disposed, which makes the call a double free on top of the walk. Binding the array needs an annotation the gir does not carry and glue that owns the whole block. That glue is Gst.Rtsp.RTSPMessage.ParseAuthCredentials of src/GstSharp.Net.Rtsp/Custom/RTSPMessageAuthCredentials.cs, which is the only caller the free has: it copies every credential of the block into a boxed wrapper of its own and then hands the block itself to gst_rtsp_auth_credentials_free exactly once, inside the member. The skip therefore stays where it is - what the ledger records is that the free has no managed spelling, not that the array it frees is unreachable.
$comment-skip-watch: GstRTSPWatch is an asynchronous RTSP connection driven from a GLib main context, and nothing in the binding can produce one. gst_rtsp_watch_new is introspectable='0', because its funcs parameter is a table of nine callbacks and its notify parameter is a bare GDestroyNotify, so the gir describes no way of calling it and no overlay can bring it back; gst_rtsp_watch_attach takes a GLib.MainContext, which is not bound either. What is emitted is therefore a public class with seven methods, an internal constructor and no producer whatsoever: every one of Reset, SendMessage, SetFlushing, SetSendBacklog, GetSendBacklog, WaitBacklogUsec and Unref is unreachable by construction, and Unref is the same unpaired release that gst_adapter_unmap is. GstRTSPWatchFuncs is the callback table of that call and nothing else; its nine fields are all callback slots, so the record is emitted as a public class with no member at all. Both are skipped rather than shipped as a dead surface a consumer would have to discover is dead. The supported way of driving a connection is Gst.Rtsp.RTSPConnection and its fully bound *Usec calls, which are synchronous and need no main context. Reviving the watch needs a hand written GstRTSPWatchFuncs of unmanaged function pointers and glue that owns the callback state for the lifetime of the watch, and the surface belongs to that glue once it is written.
$comment-skip-hand-bound-consumers: The fourteen consuming calls that shipped in 1.28.2 as hand written members, from before the generator learned the consuming argument kind. The generator now emits the same contract - mint a value for the callee, dispose the wrapper, unconditionally, which is the contract of a mini object and of a boxed value - but the hand written members stay canonical: they carry documentation the generator cannot author (what the call is for, worked examples, the bus and preroll behaviour around it), and emitting them again would declare the same member twice in one class. One way to do it: the entry points stay on the skip ledger under OverlaySkip and the hand written surface is the binding.
$comment-skip-hand-bound-values: The GValue carrying calls that shipped in 1.28.2 as hand written members, from before the planner learned the GValue projection. The generator now emits the shapes - in/ref/out over the caller's own storage, a copy or an adoption on return - but the hand written members stay canonical: they carry documentation and typing the generator cannot author (the copy-out doctrine of Structure.GetValue, the writability guard of Structure.SetValue, the typed Iterator.Items<T> that gst_iterator_next's out value backs, the ValueOrder enumeration of Global.ValueCompare over gst_value_compare, the null contract of Global.ValueSerialize over gst_value_serialize, the tag list value accessors, the GES child property family), and emitting them again would declare the same member twice in one class. Same one-way-to-do-it rule as $comment-skip-hand-bound-consumers: the entry points stay on the skip ledger under OverlaySkip and the hand written surface is the binding. gst_iterator_next is listed for its own reason on top - its out caller-allocates value would now auto-bind beside Iterator.Items<T>, and a raw Next(out Value) invites reading an iterator the typed enumerable already drives.
$comment-skip-allocator-free: gst_allocator_free is the terminal destructor of a GstMemory: it dispatches to the free function of the allocator without reading the reference count, because it is the call the mini object dispose path makes once the count has reached zero. The consuming recipe assumes the callee releases or keeps the reference it is minted - every other consuming callee unrefs it or stores it - and this one destroys the object instead, so the reference the wrapper still owns would be released on freed memory. Nothing is lost by the skip: freeing a memory block is what disposing its wrapper already does, through the unref that respects the count.
$comment-skip-toc-append: gst_toc_append_entry and gst_toc_entry_append_sub_entry consume the entry they are given and open with g_return_if_fail (gst_mini_object_is_writable (entry)) on that same argument (gsttoc.c:237 and :675). A GstTocEntry is not LOCKABLE, so writable means a reference count of exactly one, and the reference the consuming recipe mints for the callee makes the count two by construction: the check can never pass. Every call raises a GLib CRITICAL, the entry is never appended - silent data loss - and the minted reference is never consumed, so it leaks on top. A callee that asserts writability on its consumed argument is incompatible with the mint-and-dispose recipe; binding the pair needs an emission variant that hands over the wrapper's own reference instead of minting one, which does not exist.
$comment-skip-release-buffer: gst_buffer_pool_release_buffer hands the last reference of a buffer back to its pool, and everything on that path keys on the reference being the last. A buffer that fails gst_buffer_is_all_memory_writable is discarded instead of requeued, and the reset that follows runs gst_buffer_resize and metadata removal, which assert writability themselves. With the reference the wrapper still holds across the call the count is never one, so every released buffer is discarded - recycling defeated, and a pool with a fixed number of slots starves - while the reset assertions raise CRITICALs on every call, which are fatal under G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals. The member the recipe can emit is therefore not unsafe so much as useless, and it is skipped for the same missing variant as the toc pair above: releasing a buffer usefully needs the wrapper's own reference stolen, not a minted one. Nothing is lost by the skip, because disposing the wrapper is the release - the final unref runs the pool's release path with the count at exactly one, which is how every buffer a pool hands out already goes back.
$comment-skip-rtsp-range: gst_rtsp_range_parse allocates a GstRTSPTimeRange on the heap and hands the pointer out, and gst_rtsp_range_free is the release that matches it. GstRTSPTimeRange has no GType and is projected as a by-value C# struct, so nothing on the managed side can carry the heap identity the pair is about: the out parameter of parse would have to copy the structure out and free the original, which is a shape the planner does not have, and free would then be handed the address of a copy that was never allocated. Binding either half alone is worse than binding neither - a parse whose result is never freed leaks once per call, and a free that is reachable from a value the caller built on the stack is a heap corruption a caller cannot see coming. The other three functions of the record take the range by value or by reference and are bound, so what is lost is the string parser alone; gst_rtsp_range_to_string is the direction that works. Reversing this needs a projection for a heap allocated plain structure, which is a decision of its own and not one this entry makes.
$comment-skip-cursors: GstByteReader, GstByteWriter, GstBitReader and GstBitWriter are cursors over a block of memory the caller already owns, and that surface is what .NET is built around. The block is a Span<byte>, System.Buffers.Binary.BinaryPrimitives reads and writes every width in either endianness as a single inlined instruction, and System.Buffers.ArrayBufferWriter<byte> is the growing writer, where a bound cursor would cross the P/Invoke boundary once per field. The memory is already reached as a span: Gst.Buffer.Map and Gst.Base.Adapter.Map hand one out and Gst.Buffer.NewMemdup takes one back, and the one search a span cannot express on its own - the masked 32 bit start code scan, which also crosses memory an adapter holds in discontiguous pieces - is bound on Gst.Base.Adapter.MaskedScanUint32. What the bit cursors add over the byte ones is a position measured in bits with fixed width reads and nothing else; no Exp-Golomb reader appears anywhere in the girs, so they answer no codec parsing case either. What would be emitted for the four is why they are listed here rather than left alone: the record emitter binds the methods declared on a plain structure as members over a pinned instance, so leaving the four alone would offer the 140 methods they declare in GstBase-1.0.gir - 16 on GstBitReader, 19 on GstBitWriter, 66 on GstByteReader and 39 on GstByteWriter - plus the eight new and new_with_* producers that go with them, at one crossing of the P/Invoke boundary per field. Skipping them as whole types is what keeps every one of those methods out - none of them is planned, so none of them is listed in skip-report.md either. Before the emitter learned that shape the same listing held back the opposite one and the same dead end, four public value types of raw fields with no member and no producer whatsoever, which is the dead surface GstRtsp.RTSPWatch is skipped for. The listing is what pins the decision in both directions: an emitter that learns to bind a shape it used to drop decides no scope of its own here, which is what binding those 140 cursor methods with nobody deciding to would have been. Reversing it is one forceOpaque entry, which is purely additive and can be made at any point in 1.28.x.
$comment-skip-unique-list-prepend: gst_value_unique_list_prepend_value cannot work in 1.28. It delegates straight to gst_value_list_prepend_value (gstvalue.c:1180-1186), whose first statement is g_return_if_fail (GST_VALUE_HOLDS_LIST (value)) - a check for GST_TYPE_LIST exactly, which a GST_TYPE_UNIQUE_LIST value never satisfies (gstvalue.c:751). Every call is therefore a GLib CRITICAL and a no-op, whatever the caller passes. Binding it would freeze a member that can only fail, so it is skipped and goes on the upstream report backlog instead; unskipping it once the guard is fixed is purely additive. The append and concat members of the same type are unaffected: they have implementations of their own.
$comment-skip-flagset-register: gst_flagset_register is the only function of a fundamental type that is not one of the three value containers item 14 binds, and it is not a container function at all: it registers a pretty-printing sub-class of GST_TYPE_FLAG_SET. Emitting it would add a public Gst.FlagSet holder that nobody designed, on the mechanism that was frozen for the containers, so it is skipped here to keep the surface to what was reviewed. The skip is what makes it visible: before the fundamental holder existed the whole class was dropped before the census saw it, so the function appeared nowhere at all. Unskipping it is one line and purely additive.
$comment-step9-ring-buffer-positions: gst_audio_ring_buffer_set_channel_positions reads exactly buf->spec.info.channels entries out of the array it is handed, a count that is a field of the ring buffer and appears nowhere in the signature, so no annotation and no arrayOverrides entry can state the length of the array; the generator refused the callable for it. Gst.Audio.AudioRingBuffer.SetChannelPositions in src/GstSharp.Net.Audio/Custom/AudioRingBuffer.cs binds it by reading that field: it reads the acquired flag and spec.info.channels through a mirror of the instance head, refuses an unacquired ring buffer and a count above the sixty four the library has a channel order for, and refuses a span that does not hold exactly one position per channel. The positions are then copied into a sixty four entry stack buffer padded with GST_AUDIO_CHANNEL_POSITION_INVALID, the size of the position array of a GstAudioInfo, which keeps a ring buffer that changed its format between the read and the call inside that buffer. Both reads take no object lock, and neither does the C function: gst_audio_ring_buffer_acquire holds that lock across the acquire vfunc, which is where a sink sets its channel order from, so a wrapper that locked would deadlock the caller the function is written for.
$comment-step9-dsd-convert: gst_dsd_convert takes two bare guint8 blocks with no length beside them: num_dsd_bytes measures the interleaved side, while a non interleaved side is measured by the plane offsets plus num_dsd_bytes divided by num_channels, and the divisibility of num_dsd_bytes by the width of each of the two formats is a precondition the C only answers with a critical. One length parameter cannot describe two buffers of two different scales, which is what an arrayOverrides entry would have to say, so the callable is skipped and Gst.Audio.AudioGlobal.DsdConvert in src/GstSharp.Net.Audio/Custom/AudioGlobal.cs binds it with the whole precondition set checked in managed code, including the overlap of the two spans the C is not safe for.
$comment-step32-color-balance-channel-fi: GstColorBalanceChannel carries its descriptive name and its value range in three public instance fields - label, min_value and max_value - and no accessor, no property and no signal answers any of them; playback tutorial 5 reads all three. The generator cannot reach them: field emission and the field ledger both live in RecordEmitter and both walk a GirRecord, while ColorBalanceChannel is a GObject derived class, whose <field> elements ClassEmitter never looks at. That is why the three appear in no skip ledger bucket either - class fields were never counted, so no fieldSkips entry can redirect them, that key being record only. Gst.Video.ColorBalanceChannel.Label, .MinValue and .MaxValue in src/GstSharp.Net.Video/Custom/ColorBalanceChannel.cs bind them by hand, through a mirror of the instance layout in the same file: a bare GObject head, the three fields at 24, 32 and 36, and the four pointer reserved tail, for 72 bytes, which tests/GstSharp.IntegrationTests/ColorBalanceChannelFieldTests.cs asserts against the headers and against the instance size g_type_query reports. No lock is taken and none exists - the channel derives from GObject rather than from GstObject - because every implementer in GStreamer writes the three fields once while constructing the channel, before it is appended to the list gst_color_balance_list_channels answers with. Label is answered as a nullable string rather than with the throw the generator would give a field that carries no nullable annotation, which it reads as non-nullable: gst_color_balance_channel_init leaves the field NULL and nothing in the API forces an implementer to set one.
$comment-skip-scope-owned: gst_video_frame_unmap and gst_audio_buffer_unmap are the release half of a mapping the binding now takes: Gst.Video.VideoFrame.MapScope and Gst.Audio.AudioBuffer.MapScope own the GstVideoFrame and the GstAudioBuffer they were filled into and unmap it when they are disposed. The mapping travels with the scope and never with the wrapper, so a public Unmap() on the wrapper would release a mapping the wrapper does not own - Gst.Video.VideoAggregatorPad.GetPreparedFrame hands out a frame the aggregator still owns and unmaps itself, which makes that a double unmap by construction. Mapping is bound by the scopes named above; the release belongs to them and is one way, the convention the doc block of BufferNative.cs states.
$comment-skip-hand-bound-storage: Six entry points whose out parameter is storage the caller allocates and whose binding is hand written, so that the generated marshalling does not declare them a second time. gst_video_frame_map, gst_video_frame_map_id and gst_audio_buffer_map fill a mapping that has to be released again, which is a scope and not an out parameter; they are Gst.Video.VideoFrame.Map, .MapId and Gst.Audio.AudioBuffer.Map. gst_buffer_extract copies into a caller provided byte array, which is a Span destination rather than an allocation, and is Gst.Buffer.Extract. gst_query_parse_nth_allocation_param is void and leaves both of its out parameters untouched when the index is out of range, so the hand written Gst.Query.ParseNthAllocationParam range checks first and throws. gst_rtsp_transport_parse fills a GstRTSPTransport that is freed with gst_rtsp_transport_free rather than through a boxed free, so Gst.Rtsp.RTSPTransport.Parse allocates with gst_rtsp_transport_new and releases the same way.
$comment-skip-storage-siblings: Twelve entry points whose whole job is to initialise or parse into storage the caller allocates, each of which the binding already reaches through a sibling that allocates the record itself: gst_video_info_new and gst_video_info_new_from_caps, gst_video_info_dma_drm_new and gst_video_info_dma_drm_new_from_caps, gst_audio_info_new and gst_audio_info_new_from_caps, gst_dsd_info_new and gst_dsd_info_new_from_caps, gst_rtsp_transport_new, gst_sdp_message_new and gst_sdp_media_new. Binding the init and from_caps halves as well would add API parity and no reach, and every one of them would hand the caller a second way of producing the same value. gst_video_blend_scale_linear_RGBA is listed here for a different reason: its dest_buffer out parameter is left unwritten on several of its paths, so a caller cannot tell a produced buffer from an untouched one, and its own documentation declares the function bound for deprecation.
$comment-skip-hand-bound-callbacks: Four calls whose managed state has a lifetime no generated shape can express, written by hand instead. gst_buffer_new_wrapped_full and gst_memory_new_wrapped wrap memory the caller keeps: the gir calls data an (array length=size) of guint8, which is upstream's own doc comment (gstbuffer.c:991, gstallocator.c:649) and wrong twice over - the block is maxsize bytes, not size, and it must outlive the call, so no span or pinned array can stand for it - and both open with g_return_val_if_fail guards (gstallocator.c:671-672) whose NULL return gst_buffer_new_wrapped_full hands to gst_memory_lock unchecked, so the binding validates before it allocates anything. gst_install_plugins_async invokes its callback exactly once when it returns GST_INSTALL_PLUGINS_STARTED_OK and never otherwise (install-plugins.c:660-689, the child watch is registered only on that branch), so the state is freed at the call site on every other return - a condition no generic emission keys on, and the common one on Windows, where the helper is absent. gst_video_codec_frame_set_user_data runs the previous notify synchronously when it is replaced (gstvideoutils.c:77-85) and stores the GCHandle in the user_data slot the frame carries, so Gst.Video.VideoCodecFrame.GetUserData answers the binding's own pointer and is not to be dereferenced.
$comment-skip-callback-lifetime: Three callbacks whose state has no derivable lifetime at all. gst_task_pool_push: whether the pushed function ever runs depends on the pool subclass and on a GLib thread start failure that queues the item all the same (gsttaskpool.c:100-120 and 440-467; gthreadpool.c:732 queues before it reports the failure), so an unprepared default pool sets an error and never invokes, a prepared one sets the same error and invokes later, and a shared pool answers NULL with no error - nothing in the return distinguishes them. Use Gst.Task or Gst.Object.CallAsync. gst_mini_object_set_qdata: the gir gives destroy no closure index, so the planner cannot pair it with data, and untyped per object storage has no typed projection - keep the state on the managed wrapper. gst_collect_pads_add_pad: the destroy notification is handed the GstCollectData block itself rather than a user_data pointer (GstBase-1.0.gir:11863 declares no closure parameter), and it only earns its keep when the caller over allocates that block, which a managed caller cannot.
$comment-skip-callback-value: Four callback carrying calls that are skipped on value rather than for a missing mechanism. gst_debug_remove_log_function matches the function to remove by pointer identity, and a managed delegate reaches native code through a thunk whose address is not the one that was installed, so the removal can never match; use the Gst.Global.DebugAddLogFunction return instead. gst_plugin_register_static is deprecated and superseded by gst_plugin_register_static_full, which is bound and does carry user data. gst_util_array_binary_search searches an untyped block by element size, which System.Array.BinarySearch already answers in managed code. gst_tracing_register_hook takes a GObject.Callback, the untyped placeholder of the tracer subsystem's varargs hooks, which is not a closure shape at all.
$comment-skip-meta-attachment: The enumerate, remove and serialize half of the metadata surface is hand written in Custom/BufferNative.cs and Custom/MetaNative.cs, and these entries state that intent in the ledger. gst_buffer_foreach_meta hands its callback a GstMeta** whose only meaningful write is NULL (gstbuffer.c:gst_buffer_foreach_meta tests new == NULL and discards any other pointer the callback stores), which is a keep/remove/stop decision rather than an inout parameter; no ArgumentKind describes it, and the trampoline also has to invalidate the wrapper of a removed item and re-throw a managed exception after the walk. gst_meta_serialize_simple takes a GByteArray* sink, of which the girs carry five occurrences in total, and its generated sibling Meta.Serialize(GstByteArrayInterface) could not be called outside a serialize callback until Gst.ByteArrayInterface got a public constructor, which src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/ByteArrayInterface.cs now gives it; the hand written Meta.Serialize() owns a GByteArray for the length of the call and answers a byte[], and the sibling is what appends several serialisations to one array. gst_buffer_add_audio_meta sizes its offsets array by info->channels, a field of another parameter, which arrayOverrides cannot redirect to (it only names another parameter). gst_buffer_iterate_meta and gst_buffer_iterate_meta_filtered are introspectable='0' in the gir and never reach the classifier, so they get no entry on this list; both are on the hand bound list instead, where the ledger files them under HandBound rather than under NotIntrospectable, because Gst.Buffer.IterateMeta imports the first by hand and does the filtering of the second in managed code.
$comment-skip-aggregate-params: gst_meta_api_type_aggregate_params takes GstStructure** and the gir declares GstStructure*, so the shipped Meta.ApiTypeAggregateParams passed a live structure where the library writes a pointer: the in-tree aggregator (gstvideometa.c:gst_video_meta_api_params_aggregator, registered at :202) assigns *aggregated_params on every path and never reads it, so each historical call overwrote the first eight bytes - the GType header - of the caller's own GstStructure and leaked the copy it had just made. The correction cannot be spelled as an annotationOverride: MarshalPlanner.OverriddenDirection accepts an out direction only for a pointer to a plain structure, to a GValue, to a scalar or to an enumeration, and GstStructure is a boxed record, so the entry would be reported as GEN0017 and ignored. The call is therefore skipped and written by hand, with the out parameter it always had and with the shipped signature kept beside it as an [Obsolete] bridge that throws: the parameter is passed by reference now, which is a binary break the package validation baseline does not see (it compares member signatures without the ref kind), and the 1.28.x promise is what keeps the old overload alive rather than the gate. gst_meta_api_type_set_params_aggregator is skipped with it: its callback typedef GstAllocationMetaParamsAggregator carries the same GstStructure** with no direction attribute at all, and MarshalPlanner.PlanCallbackCore rejects any callback parameter whose gir direction is not 'in' before an override is consulted - and MarshalPlanner.IsPointerToHandlePointer now refuses that GstStructure** ahead of the direction test in any case, because two stars over a boxed record is the pointer to a handle pointer shape, which is refused for a callback argument and for a signal argument as well as for an in parameter - so neither half of that pair is expressible today. It is meta authorship in any case - the aggregator is only useful to code that registers a new meta API type - and it stays deferred, now on its own: gst_meta_register and gst_meta_info_new are bound, see $comment-hand-bound-meta-authorship. Both annotation faults are on the upstream report backlog.

$comment-step9-video-vbi-lines: gst_video_vbi_encoder_write_line and gst_video_vbi_parser_add_line take one bare guint8 line with no length beside it, and the number of bytes they touch follows from the format and the pixel width that were handed to gst_video_vbi_encoder_new or gst_video_vbi_parser_new: both objects are opaque and expose no getter for either, so nothing in the signature and nothing on the instance can tell a caller or the generator how long the line has to be. $comment-skip-list-free: Three calls whose whole body is the release of a native list that managed code never holds. gst_plugin_feature_list_free (gstpluginfeature.c) walks the list with gst_object_unref per feature and then g_list_free; gst_plugin_list_free (gstplugin.c) is the same shape with GST_PLUGIN_CAST; gst_discoverer_stream_info_list_free (gstdiscoverer-types.c) is the same with gst_discoverer_stream_info_unref, which gstdiscoverer.h:61 defines as g_object_unref. The planner refuses a transfer-full GObject list on its own; the entries are here so the ledger states the intent rather than reporting an unexplained unsupported signature.
$comment-skip-iterator-list: gst_iterator_new_list takes GList** and keeps it: gstiterator.c stores result->orig = list and result->list = *list, then re-reads *orig on every resync, so the address of the caller's own list variable has to stay valid and mutable for the life of the iterator. $comment-skip-hand-bound-select-streams: gst_event_new_select_streams is hand bound in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/Event.cs:183-226 and stays that way. It is the one call in the family that refuses an empty list - gstevent.c opens with g_return_val_if_fail (streams != NULL, NULL) and copies every id into a GValue of the payload structure - so the shipped member answers an empty sequence with ArgumentException before anything native is allocated. $comment-skip-wait-async: gst_clock_id_wait_async is hand bound as Gst.Clock.IdWaitAsync in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/Clock.cs, because the C function only takes the destroy notification over once it has written it onto the entry. gstclock.c assigns func, user_data and destroy_data onto the entry immediately before it dispatches to the wait_async of the clock class, and three exits are taken in front of that assignment: GST_CLOCK_ERROR when the entry lost its clock, GST_CLOCK_UNSUPPORTED when the class carries no wait_async, and GST_CLOCK_BADTIME when the requested time is invalid, which invokes func once and returns without ever having seen destroy_data. The generated shape allocates the GCHandle of the callback and hands the destroy notification over unconditionally, so those three leak it. Whatever the dispatch itself answers leaves the state with the entry, which releases it when the entry is freed - GST_CLOCK_OK, but also the GST_CLOCK_UNSCHEDULED of an entry that was unscheduled beforehand and the GST_CLOCK_ERROR of a clock that could not start its waiting thread, where a release by the binding would be a double free. The hand written member is the generated body with two additions: it holds a reference to the clock of the entry across the call, which leaves the GST_CLOCK_ERROR in front of the assignment as the only one that can come back with no clock, and it frees the handle on GST_CLOCK_BADTIME, on GST_CLOCK_UNSUPPORTED and on that clockless GST_CLOCK_ERROR alone.
$comment-skip-register-custom: gst_meta_register_custom is hand bound as Gst.Meta.RegisterCustom in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/Meta.cs, for the same reason as gst_clock_id_wait_async above. gstmeta.c only writes custom_transform_func, custom_transform_user_data and custom_transform_destroy_notify onto the implementation block once that block exists, so neither of the two failures in front of it - an API type that could not be registered, and an implementation block that could not be allocated - has anything to release when it jumps to the exit that answers NULL. The registration that follows them, gst_meta_info_register, answers NULL as well when the type of the implementation is invalid, and g_frees the block without ever running the destroy notification that is written on it by then: the only call of that notification walks the table of registrations the block never entered. The generated shape allocates the GCHandle of the transform function first and reports the NULL as an InvalidOperationException, so the handle is leaked by the throw on all three. The hand written member is the generated body with one addition: the handle is released before the exception is raised. gst_meta_register_custom_simple is a different entry point that takes no callback and stays generated.
$comment-skip-hand-written-callback-type: Two callback types whose delegate is written by hand. Each needs an entry here because the generated twin would otherwise be emitted beside it: a callback type at least one hand bound consumer takes is planned on that consumer's behalf, so skipping the consumer no longer takes the type down with it. GstBusSyncHandler: the trampoline of Gst.Bus.SetSyncHandler releases the reference of the poster when the handler answers GST_BUS_DROP, because managed code cannot, and the hand written delegate is where that contract is documented; a generated twin would declare the same delegate a second time and carry the gir prose, which says nothing about it. GstInstallPluginsResultFunc: gst_install_plugins_async invokes it exactly once and only when the call answered GST_INSTALL_PLUGINS_STARTED_OK, which is the reason that call is hand bound at all, and the hand written delegate documents that alongside the main context it runs on. Both entries keep the generated surface from declaring a type the hand written one already owns. The six GstMeta callback types - Gst.MetaInitFunction, Gst.MetaFreeFunction, Gst.MetaTransformFunction, Gst.MetaSerializeFunction, Gst.MetaDeserializeFunction and Gst.MetaClearFunction - were listed here too, as a guard rather than as a correction, and they are listed no longer: they matched nothing, which is what GEN0056 reports since the diagnostic exists. They are declared by hand in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/MetaAuthor.cs with the projections the generator cannot reach for, a ReadOnlySpan over the data and size pair of the deserialisation and a ref byte for the version the serialisation writes. Only three of the six have a callable consumer in the gir at all - the init, free and transform arguments of gst_meta_register, which is hand bound below - and PlanCallbackArgument refuses all three for want of a closure index, the gir giving none of them a scope, a closure or a destroy. Should a later gir refresh annotate them, that hand bound consumer would claim its three types back and the generated twins would collide with the hand written ones; the collision is a build failure of the same gate rather than a silent one, and re-adding the six entries is the fix. A third delegate is written by hand without an entry here, and the difference is what a consumer's claim can and cannot do: a hand bound consumer keeps its callback type generated only while the planner can still plan that type, and MarshalPlanner.IsPointerToScalar refuses GstAudioBaseSinkCustomSlavingCallback on its requested_skew argument. There is no generated twin of it to keep out, so Gst.Audio.AudioBaseSinkCustomSlavingHandler and the obsolete AudioBaseSinkCustomSlavingCallback beside it are declared by hand and this list says nothing about them; see $comment-skip-slaving-callback.
$comment-skip-fixate: gst_caps_fixate is hand bound as Gst.Caps.Fixate in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/Caps.cs. $comment-skip-with-properties: gst_element_factory_create_with_properties and gst_element_factory_make_with_properties are hand bound as Gst.ElementFactory.CreateWithProperties and Gst.ElementFactory.MakeWithProperties in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/ElementFactory.cs. $comment-skip-transcoder-parse: gst_transcoder_message_parse_error and gst_transcoder_message_parse_warning are hand bound as Gst.Transcoder.TranscoderMessageExtensions.ParseError and ParseWarning in src/GstSharp.Net.Transcoder/Custom/TranscoderMessageExtensions.cs. Both read their fields through PARSE_MESSAGE_FIELD (gsttranscoder.c:1378-1385), whose miss branch is g_error ("Could not parse field from structure: %s"), and g_error aborts the process. That is not a theoretical branch: the transcoder posts an error message with the error field alone on four paths - a clock loss it could not recover from at :647, a state the pipeline refused to change to at :737, and the two synchronous failures of gst_transcoder_run_async, no encoding profile at :1024 and a pipeline that would not start at :1037 - and none of them attaches the issue-details field the second half of the parse then demands, so the generated call would abort on the very messages the API exists to report. The optional error out parameter has the same shape from the other side: the gir marks it optional, so a generated overload that passed NULL for it would abort on the first field instead of the second. The hand written pair reads the structure of the message itself, answers the error as a GException value copied out of the boxed GError and the details as an owned copy of the structure or as null when the field is absent, and raises ArgumentException for a message that is not a transcoder message or does not carry the field of the parse that was asked for. The three sibling parses - duration, position and state - post their one field on every path and stay generated.

$comment-skip-rtsp-server: Seven GstRtspServer entry points that cannot be offered as the gir spells them. gst_rtsp_client_set_send_func and gst_rtsp_client_set_send_messages_func are unreachable on every path that exists: gst_rtsp_client_attach installs do_send_messages on every client (rtsp-client.c:5366-5368) and client-connected fires before that attach (rtsp-server.c:1106 against :1133), so the first call always reaches its g_assert (rtsp-client.c:4828, :4783) and the second is silently overwritten a moment later. gst_rtsp_token_writable_structure hands the structure of the token out by pointer to be written through, and a plain structure is projected by value, so the writes of a caller would land in a copy the token never sees; gst_rtsp_token_set_string and gst_rtsp_token_set_bool are the writing path that works. gst_rtsp_thread_pool_get_thread, gst_rtsp_thread_stop and gst_rtsp_media_prepare are hand written in src/GstSharp.Net.RtspServer/Custom with a stop based lifetime, because the release of a pooled thread is not an unreference: one get_thread hands out one reference and one reused count - a thread made for the call starts at both (rtsp-thread-pool.c:107, :119-131 through :415) and a recycled one is reused, which adds one of each (:151-153, reached from :455-463) - exactly one gst_rtsp_thread_stop releases both - straight away, or through the destroy notification of the idle source that quits the loop (:182-189) - and an unreference without a stop leaks the OS thread, whose own worker holds a reference of its own until the loop quits (:474 for a client thread, :486 for a media one), while a second stop on one reference is a use after free. $comment-skip-param-spec-records: Gst.ParamSpecFraction and Gst.ParamSpecArray are hand bound in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom instead of generated, next to the sixteen GLib derived classes of src/GstSharp.Net/Core/GObject/ParamSpecTypes.cs. The shells had no public surface, so removing them takes nothing away.
$comment-skip-event-full-function: gst_pad_set_event_full_function_full is hand bound as Gst.Pad.SetEventFullFunction in src/GstSharp.Net/Custom/Pad.cs, because unsetting the handler is a state the C leaves broken. gstpad.c:1979-1984 writes GST_PAD_EVENTFULLFUNC (pad) = event and then GST_PAD_EVENTFUNC (pad) = event_wrap unconditionally, so passing NULL leaves the wrapper installed as the plain event function of the pad over a full function pointer that is now NULL, and the next event dereferences it. $comment-force-opaque-sdp: The payload structures of an SDP message are plain C structures that the library hands out by pointer, and every accessor of theirs takes or returns such a pointer. A plain structure is projected as a value type, which copies it, and the methods declared on it are dropped for exactly that reason, so the media, attribute, origin, connection, bandwidth, time, zone and key surface of the module is unreachable. Keeping the eight of them behind a pointer binds it: the wrapper addresses the storage the message owns, so a read sees the message and a write reaches it. As on every other opaque record, 'Free' and 'Uninit' are public on the wrappers; neither may be called on an instance that a message still owns.
$comment-force-opaque-transport: GstRTSPTransport is the same shape as the SDP payload structures and gets the same answer. It is a plain C structure the library hands out by pointer, gst_rtsp_transport_new allocates one and writes the address into an out parameter, and every accessor takes such a pointer, so projecting it as a value type drops as_text, free, get_media_type, get_manager and get_mime and leaves a structure whose destination and source fields are bare gchar pointers that no caller can read. Keeping it behind a pointer binds that surface and stops the two string fields from being offered as raw addresses. What stays unbound is init and parse, whose transport parameter is caller-allocates='1': a record bound behind a handle is one pointer wide, so the call would write a whole GstRTSPTransport past the end of what it is given, and they move to the CallerAllocates bucket exactly as gst_sdp_media_init and gst_sdp_message_init did. The range structures keep their value projection: GstRTSPRange is embedded by value four times in GstRTSPTransport and GstRTSPTime and GstRTSPTime2 are embedded in GstRTSPTimeRange, so forcing any of them behind a pointer would demote the structures that contain them, and their fields are plain integers that a copy reads correctly.
$comment-force-opaque-meta: A GstMeta lives inside the buffer that carries it. gst_buffer_get_meta and the typed gst_buffer_get_*_meta accessors hand out a pointer into the storage of that buffer, the lifetime of the metadata is the lifetime of the buffer, and a write to one of its fields is meant to reach the copy the buffer holds. A value projection can only ever snapshot it, and all three of the things a metadata item is for are lost by the copy: a read produces a structure that stopped tracking the buffer the moment it was taken, a write reaches a stack temporary that is discarded when the call returns, and the pointer identity that gst_buffer_remove_meta keys on is gone, which also takes with it any chance that what gst_buffer_iterate_meta and gst_buffer_foreach_meta walk over is the metadata of the buffer rather than a copy of it. That third one is not a prediction, it is the fault gst_buffer_remove_meta was skipped for above, which '$comment-skip-identity' records and which these entries cure. GstMeta itself is the header every metadata structure embeds by value as its first field, so the twenty two are forced together: keeping the header behind a pointer while the structures that carry it stay values, or the other way round, is the demotion the range structures of GstRTSPTransport are deliberately left by value to avoid. What the entries buy on their own is the correct foundation - a wrapper that addresses the metadata of the buffer instead of a copy of it - and the methods the gir declares on the records, which a plain structure drops. GstMetaInfo and GstVideoMeta are opaque already and are unaffected. The typed field accessors and the gst_buffer_add_*_meta, iterate and foreach attachment surface are purely additive on top of this shape and arrive later in the series.
$comment-force-opaque-static: A GstStaticCaps is a cache, not a value. gst_static_caps_get parses the string of the structure the first time it is asked and writes the GstCaps it built back through the pointer it was handed, under a lock, so that every later call on the same storage hands out that one caps; gst_static_caps_cleanup clears the field again. The identity of the storage is the whole contract, and a value projection can only snapshot it: the write back reaches a stack temporary that is discarded when the call returns, the cache the library meant to fill stays empty, and the reference the parse took is leaked once per call. GstStaticPadTemplate is the structure an element factory keeps in its own static storage, embeds a GstStaticCaps by value, and carries the same fault, so the two are forced together exactly as GstMeta and the structures that embed it are. The fields of the two are a cached pointer no caller may write and a name a caller has no way of supplying - a static pad template is declared in C by a macro no binding can reach - so neither structure was ever constructible from managed code, and what the value projection offered was the raw addresses of storage nobody could produce. $comment-force-opaque-resampler: A GstVideoResampler owns four blocks of memory that only gst_video_resampler_clear can give back. gst_video_resampler_init allocates the offset, phase, n_taps and taps arrays for the sizes it is asked for and writes their addresses into the structure; clear frees all four and zeroes it again. $comment-direction-writeback: The gir has one spelling for a pointer to a plain structure whether the C function reads it or fills it: a bare 'GstVideoAlignment*' with no direction attribute on it. Its unmap is 'ref' rather than 'in' because it has to be handed the info that map wrote and because meta->map and meta->unmap are function pointers of the metadata item that any element may replace, so what runs on the other side of the call is not one fixed implementation. gst_buffer_unmap and gst_memory_unmap are the deliberate exceptions: their parameter is non-const as well, but the implementation behind them is fixed - a memory unmap through the allocator of the block - and reads the info without writing it, so passing the value is correct there and they keep the signature they shipped with. The correction is refused for anything but a pointer to a plain structure, to a GValue, to a scalar or to an enumeration; a pointer to a scalar is what the RTCP XR readers of $comment-xr-out are corrected with and a pointer to an enumeration is what the two SDES entry readers of $comment-sdes-out are corrected with, while a handle, a string or an array still has an out projection of its own.
$comment-direction-poll: The whole gst_poll file descriptor family takes a 'GstPollFD*' the library keeps state in. GstPollFD carries a private 'idx' beside the descriptor, which is the position of the descriptor inside the set: gst_poll_add_fd writes it after appending, and the lookup every other call starts with reads it as a hint, verifies it against the descriptor it names and rewrites it when the hint was stale. Passing a copy hands that state to a stack temporary that the member discards, so the cache the library maintains in the caller's structure is thrown away once per call and nothing the caller holds ever learns the index it was given. Every one of the eleven is turned into a 'ref' for it, which is the storage the C function was written to be handed. One gap stays and is not this correction's to close: GST_POLL_FD_INIT initialises idx to -1 and the gir marks the field private, so a default-constructed Gst.PollFD starts with an idx of 0 rather than -1. The lookup validates the hint against the descriptor before it trusts it, so a wrong index is recovered from rather than acted on. Gst.PollFD.Init, which the record emitter now binds along with the other methods of a plain structure, is the call that sets the descriptor and the index the way GST_POLL_FD_INIT does; a default-constructed value still starts with an idx of 0, so a caller that means the initialised state calls Init on a variable of its own.
$comment-fixed-arrays: Two members pass a pointer to one element where the C function unconditionally writes four of them: GST_VIDEO_MAX_PLANES for the one and GST_VIDEO_MAX_COMPONENTS for the other. The size is a fact about the C implementation that no gir annotation carries, so it is stated here; the parameter is then planned as an out of an [InlineArray] struct of that length, nested in the declaring type and named after the parameter, so the storage is the size the callee writes, the caller cannot supply less, and nothing is allocated per call.
$comment-transfer-prepare-read: gst_audio_ring_buffer_prepare_read hands out a pointer into the ring buffer's own segment memory - 'a pointer to memory where the data from segment can be found', in the words of its C documentation, borrowed for as long as the buffer stays acquired. The override states the borrow; the member keeps copying, which is the right projection of memory whose lifetime belongs to the device thread.

The return value of a virtual method is the one place an entry may state that a type the gir spells as a bare pointer is an array after all, and only when it names the element type and the length together: a slot upstream marks introspectable="0" carries no annotation to correct. $comment-field-skips: Record fields that carry API in C and are answered by something other than an accessor of their own, keyed by the c:type of the record and the gir name of the field. A field of a reserved ABI union is addressed by the record it grows, with the union and the structure inside it transparent, the same way its accessor would be named. The entry keeps the field out of the field ledger of the skip report and keeps the generator from emitting an accessor for it, which is what makes it the answer to a name a hand written member already carries. Exactly one of 'exposedBy' and 'handBound' has to be stated, and the check is exclusive; a key that matches no field of an emitted record, an entry that states neither, and an entry that states both are all reported as GEN0025.

'nullable: false' says the field never holds the null pointer, which a gir cannot spell on a <field> at all, and emits the accessor of it non nullable. 'name' is the stem the member that reads the field is named after, in place of the one the field name derives, and the rule that decides between a property and a Get method works on it unchanged. 'accessor: false' holds the field back from the accessors: the pointer stays on the mirror and the field stays on the ledger under its own shape, and it excludes the other two, which may be stated together. A key that matches no field an accessor would be emitted for, an entry that states nothing or only the default, an empty name and a name the field derives anyway are all reported as GEN0026. $comment-field-annotation-accessor: Two reasons hold a field back below, and each entry states its own. One is a pointer the header keeps to the implementation of the structure, where the copy the boxed wrapper takes aliases what the owner frees. One is storage the user fills and hands to the library, which takes it over and would refuse to write a list a reference of ours made unwritable. Two shapes are refused by the generator rather than by an entry here, and no overlay may lift either. A field newer than the support floor is one: the structure an older library allocates does not hold it. A mini object a record embeds by value is the other: the field starts at the address of the record it is declared in, so the accessor would be an identity cast that the remark of an embedded record would describe as a copy.

$comment-instance-fields: The instance fields of a GObject class that the generator exposes through an accessor of its own, keyed the way 'fieldSkips' is. A wrapper mirrors no part of the instance it holds, so every field of a class is out of reach by default and the ledger counts the whole of them; an entry here is the exception. 'lock' is the lock or locks the library rewrites the field under, printed into the generated remark, and managed code can take none of them: each is a C macro over storage inside GstPad, over the non recursive object lock, or over a mutex of the base class itself. 'overrides' is therefore required: it names the gir virtual methods the base class calls on the streaming thread, where the pad holds the stream lock around the call, which is the window a read is consistent in. '$comment' names the header file and line both claims were read from. An optional 'name' renames the accessor, and it has to be an identifier. The class has to be on 'subclassable': a class with no subclassing surface has no override to read the field inside, so there is no window to state. Wave 1 admits one shape, an embedded GstSegment, whose copy is flat and owns no pointer, so a read outside the window is a torn value and never unsafe; a pointer, a callback, a scalar, another embedded structure, a field above the support floor and a field the gir marks private without an optional 'headerPublic' are all refused, and the refusal is an error because the accessor is public surface. A key naming a nested union of an instance structure matches no field at all, because a gir keeps a union out of the field list, and a class that grew one carries no mirror: both are errors as well. So is a field the mirror cannot lay out - a type the closed table does not name, or a bitfield. 'headerPublic' names the header line that documents such a field: it corrects a scanner artefact, where a structure opens '/*< private >*/' and switches to '/*< protected >*/', which the scanner does not read as public, so every field behind it comes out private; it never reaches generated code, it is refused when it is empty, and it is refused as stale once the gir marks the field public, which retires it. Reserved padding, whose name the girs open with an underscore, is refused whatever a key says. Citations are relative to the GStreamer 1.28 monorepo, subprojects/.

$comment-subclassable: The classes a managed subclass may derive from. It is an allowlist rather than everything the girs declare: a class here gets a class struct mirror, a generated *.Subclass.cs with one OnX member per bindable slot, and its whole parent chain gets mirrors as well, because a mirror embeds the one of its parent by value. A class that is only on the chain - Gst.Object - gets the mirror and no managed surface. Stage 2a is the seven Gst and GstBase classes and the seven GstAudio and GstVideo classes that are not codec bases; Stage 2b adds GstBase.BaseParse and the four codec bases, GstAudio.AudioDecoder, GstAudio.AudioEncoder, GstVideo.VideoDecoder and GstVideo.VideoEncoder; stage 3c adds the seven GES classes a managed source and the clip that builds it are made of, and pulls GES.Container in behind them as a chain only mirror. Stage 3d adds the six GES classes a managed effect and the clip that carries it are made of - Operation, BaseEffect, Effect, OperationClip, BaseEffectClip and EffectClip - none of which declares a slot of its own, so they add mirrors and registrations and no OnX member.
$comment-skip-virtuals: The slots of a subclassable class that carry no managed surface, with the reason the skip ledger prints. The mirror still lays every one of them out - a class struct is an ABI and not a menu - so what is removed is the OnX member, its chain-up and its trampoline. A slot the planner cannot project is not listed here: it is reported by the run as UnsupportedSignature, so a shape that becomes bindable stops being skipped without anybody editing this file. A key may also name one hand-bound slot of a chain-only mirror - a class that is not subclassable but whose mirror lays the slots out - which is how a slot that is written by hand for the classes below it states so instead of printing the fixed 'not subclassable' reason. That width has a price GEN0029 cannot pay for the reader: taking a class off the 'subclassable' list above does not make its entries here stale, because the mirror of a class on a chain stays and the entries go on reading as ledger reasons for it. Removing a class from that list therefore means re-reading its entries here by hand - the run has no way to tell an entry that was written for the subclassing surface from one written for a chain-only mirror.

$comment-vfunc-defaults: What a chain-up does when the parent class leaves the slot NULL, which is the behaviour the base class documents for that case. Every entry was read out of the C implementation of 1.28.6 - the guard around the call and the value the caller falls back to - and the per class tables of the stage-2 verification pass name the line. A value that opens with { is a statement block the null branch consists of, written out verbatim, which is how a slot that hands one of its arguments back, or one whose answer is read off the instance, says so; everything else is an expression the branch answers. A handle is answered raw, because the static chain-up hands handles on without a wrapper. GES.TimelineElement::set_parent is a plain default of that kind: ges_timeline_element_set_parent guards the NULL slot and goes on to adopt the parent and answer TRUE (ges-timeline-element.c:995-1000), and only the video source family fills the slot (ges-video-source.c:261, ges-video-test-source.c:172), so true is what the library itself answers for the empty slot every other class leaves behind. A slot with no entry has no value a chain-up could invent: Gst.Element::change_state is never NULL in any class of the chain; Gst.Bin::handle_message and every other void slot is a no-op the emitter writes by itself; GstBase.BaseTransform::get_unit_size and GstBase.Aggregator::aggregate are called unguarded, so a subclass has to implement them; GstBase.BaseTransform::transform_ip is the one entry that is a reading rather than a fallback the base class takes: gstbasetransform.c:2201-2219 leaves GST_FLOW_OK for a NULL slot in passthrough mode and never calls the slot outside of it, where it dispatches to transform or answers NOT_SUPPORTED, so Ok is the answer of a chain-up that says 'the buffer is unchanged' and not a C default. Gst.DeviceProvider::start is the other reading of that kind: no class of the chain implements the slot and the fallback the C takes for a NULL one is the unguarded klass->probe call of gstdeviceprovider.c:476-481, which is a crash for a managed provider and not a value, so true is what 'nothing below the override refuses to start' reads as rather than what the base class does. And GstBase.BaseSink::render_list answers no value at all when it is NULL - the base class splits the list and pushes every buffer through render instead, which is a dispatch strategy and not a result. The lifecycle slots of GstBase.BaseParse, of the four codec bases, of GstAudio.AudioFilter, GstVideo.VideoFilter and GstVideo.VideoSink, together with GES.Source::select_pad and GstBase.BaseTransform::filter_meta, are plain guarded defaults of the first kind, read at 1.28.6 and again at the 1.24.0 floor, where every guard and every fallback is the same. Three of them are readings of a third kind: GstVideo.VideoDecoder::flush, GstVideo.VideoDecoder::reset and GstVideo.VideoEncoder::reset are called bare and what they answer is discarded (gstvideodecoder.c:1049-1055, gstvideoencoder.c:764-767), so true is what 'nothing below the override refused' reads as and not a value the C ever holds; and GstVideo.VideoDecoder::finish and ::drain answer Ok as the value the base class leaves in place for an empty slot, which is Ok when the parse step before it succeeded (gstvideodecoder.c:1180-1196). GstAudio.AudioEncoder::set_format has no entry on purpose: gst_audio_encoder_sink_setcaps refuses an empty slot with g_return_val_if_fail before it reaches the guarded call (gstaudioencoder.c:1464, :1504), which is a critical and not a default, so the registration requires the slot instead (VfuncEmitter.cs BaseRules). GES.TimelineElement::get_layer_priority is a block of the second kind: ges_timeline_element_get_layer_priority answers self->priority for an empty slot (ges-timeline-element.c:2439-2440, the same at the 1.24.0 floor), which is what ges_timeline_element_get_priority reads (:1444-1449), so the branch calls that entry point on the instance; only a direct TimelineElement subclass reaches it, because GESClip and GESTrackElement fill the slot (ges-clip.c:2678, ges-track-element.c:493).
$comment-vfunc-doc-notes: The part of the contract of a slot that neither the gir nor its marshalling states, as one sentence per slot appended to the remarks of the generated OnX and ChainUpX members. What belongs here is what a reader would otherwise have to read the C implementation to learn.

A child built with new has no asset: it never gets an nleobject, ges_layer_add_clip_full removes it from the clip again (ges-layer.c:781-808), and splitting or pasting the clip aborts the process on g_assert (asset) (ges-timeline-element.c:1675). vfuncDocNotes.GES.Source::create_source: The bin of the source adds the answer and takes a reference of its own (gst_bin_add sinks it, ges-source.c:205, ges-audio-source.c:148 for an audio source), so the wrapper keeps working and no reference is added on the way out. The trampoline hands the handle on and moves no reference, so a wrapper you answer keeps the reference it already owns and may be disposed after the call or read back from the track element instead of being kept. Answer an element that has no parent yet and keep no extra reference to it: add_failure unrefs both the answer and the nlesource when the bin refuses it (ges-track-element.c:1073-1078). Answering null, or throwing, which the trampoline turns into a null answer, would leave the track element with an nleobject it no longer owns: child_failure unrefs it while it is still floating (ges-track-element.c:1022, 1066-1070), the composition sinks the last reference and frees the object when the element is removed, and dispose unrefs it again. GES 1.28.6 does that; the binding therefore answers an identity element in place of a null one and reports the substitution through the exception trap, so nothing feeds the substitute, the source produces no data and the pipeline cannot preroll. Answer a real element, or do not declare the slot. For a VideoSource or an AudioSource subclass no ancestor implements the slot: there is nothing below to chain up to, and ChainUpCreateSource throws.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.Source::select_pad: This slot may run on the thread that emits the pad-added of the sub element (ges-source.c:126, 190, 240), which is a streaming thread when the source is a dynamic one. GESSource leaves the slot empty and the caller accepts the pad for an empty one - only a slot that answers false makes it ignore the pad (ges-source.c:126). The classes of the library that fill it, the audio and the video uri source (ges-audio-uri-source.c:157, ges-video-uri-source.c:334), are outside the subclassable set, so a chain-up answers true below a managed audio or video source rather than throwing.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::get_layer_priority: GESTimelineElement leaves this slot empty and ges_timeline_element_get_layer_priority answers the priority of the element itself for an empty one (ges-timeline-element.c:2439-2440) - not GES_TIMELINE_ELEMENT_NO_LAYER_PRIORITY, which is what GESClip and GESTrackElement answer when they are in no layer and no parent (ges-clip.c:1551-1559, ges-track-element.c:162-168). Those two classes fill the slot, so a chain-up below a clip or a track element runs their implementation; directly below GESTimelineElement it answers Priority rather than throwing.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::list_children_prope: The block is sorted by property name by the caller of the slot (ges-timeline-element.c:2260), so the order an override answers in is not the order a reader sees.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::lookup_child: Both out parameters are owned by the caller on the true path and left untouched on the false one (ges-timeline-element.c:257-289): the caller unreferences the child and the specification unconditionally once the answer is true (ges-timeline-element.c:2022-2023), so neither may be null there - an override that leaves one empty is reported through the exception trap and the slot answers false instead. The child may be the element itself, which is what the registration allows (ges-timeline-element.c:909-910).
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::paste: The caller takes a reference of its own from the answer (g_object_ref_sink, ges-timeline-element.c:2416, ges-timeline.c:3324), so the wrapper keeps working and no reference is added on the way out. Keep no extra reference to it.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::set_child_property: The element this runs on may be the owner of an inherited child property rather than the element the public call named (ges-timeline-element.c:821-823). The value may arrive as a string for a specification of another type as well, because the by name setters go through gst_util_set_object_arg (ges-timeline-element.c:204-212): read the type of the value before a typed getter, or chain up, which handles that case.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::set_duration: The C slot may answer -1 for 'the change is already applied', but the only class that does is GESGroup (ges-group.c:317), which is outside the subclassable set, so the bool means what it says here.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::set_max_duration: This slot runs inside g_object_new, for the CONSTRUCT max-duration property (ges-timeline-element.c:543-547) and before the name is set, so an instance the native side constructs is seen half built.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::set_parent: A null parent is the removal of the element from the parent it had. Only the video source family implements this slot (ges-video-source.c:261, ges-video-test-source.c:172), and the caller treats an empty one as success (ges-timeline-element.c:995-1000), so a chain-up answers true below every other class rather than throwing.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::deep_copy: The copy is a fresh instance of the same managed type this element has, and it already carries every readable and writable property of the class that is neither construct-only nor parent, timeline or name - the ones a managed type installed included - because ges_timeline_element_copy copies them before it reaches this slot (ges-timeline-element.c:1672, 1677-1691). What belongs here is the state that lives outside properties; chain up first, then copy it. The copy arrives floating and stays floating: the wrapper settles nothing and takes a reference of its own, so the caller still holds its floating reference and drops it without ever sinking it. An override must not add the copy to a container or a layer, must not paste it, and should not keep its wrapper beyond the call - a kept wrapper defers the finalize of the copy and buys nothing. A subclass defined without a wrapper factory - the non-generic DefineSubclass, which registers no IManagedSubclass<TSelf> - has no fabrication for the copy, so no OnDeepCopy call is made at all for it and the base class makes the copy alone.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TimelineElement::set_start: The C slot may answer -1 for 'the change is already applied', but the only class that does is GESGroup (ges-group.c:317), which is outside the subclassable set, so the bool means what it says here.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TrackElement::create_element: The same rules as GES.Source::create_source: the bin of the nleobject adds the answer and takes a reference of its own (gst_bin_add sinks it, ges-track-element.c:1026-1038), so the wrapper keeps working and no reference is added on the way out. Answer an element that has no parent yet and keep no extra reference to it. Answering null, or throwing, which the trampoline turns into a null answer, would leave the nleobject of the track element over-released and freed while dispose still unrefs it (ges-track-element.c:1022, 1066-1070, and the composition sinks what is left) in GES 1.28.6, so the binding answers an identity element in its place and reports the substitution through the exception trap. Answer a real element, or do not declare the slot.
vfuncDocNotes.GES.TrackElement::create_gnl_object: Return what the chain-up answered: set_asset references the object once, and only while priv->nleobject is still NULL (ges-track-element.c:306-309), and dispose drops that one reference again (ges-track-element.c:269-271).
vfuncDocNotes.Gst.Bin::handle_message: The override takes the message over: chaining up passes it on and disposes it, and an override that does neither drops the message, which is what makes this the hook for swallowing or rewriting what children post. Copy the message to keep it beyond the call.
vfuncDocNotes.Gst.DeviceProvider::start: Every managed device provider has to declare this slot or ProbeOverride, which DefineSubclass checks for: gst_device_provider_start calls klass->probe with no NULL check when klass->start is NULL (gstdeviceprovider.c:476-481), so a provider that declares neither would end a Start call in a call through a NULL function pointer. The registration refuses a provider that declares neither instead of letting it crash. With this slot declared, Start never reaches probe: the unguarded call is the branch taken for a NULL start alone, so OnProbe of such a provider is reached by GetDevices on a provider that is not started and by nothing else. No class in the chain installs a start of its own - gstdeviceprovider.h:169-184 declares the slot and the base class leaves it NULL - so a chain-up reaches nothing and answers true, meaning nothing below the override refuses to start, and a provider with no work to do may leave OnStart alone. Answer false to refuse to start; there is no error channel, the C slot is a plain gboolean. Withdraw what was already announced before answering false, and before letting an exception out, which the trampoline reports and turns into false: the base class leaves those devices parented to the provider until it is disposed, and it calls no stop for a provider that never started (gstdeviceprovider.c:497-500, 536-543). The slot runs with the start lock of the provider held (gstdeviceprovider.c:466-506): calling IsStarted, GetDevices, Start or Stop on the same provider from inside the override deadlocks on that non recursive mutex. DeviceAdd, DeviceRemove, DeviceChanged, HideProvider and GetBus are safe, because they take the object lock or no lock at all.
vfuncDocNotes.Gst.DeviceProvider::stop: This slot is optional and one of start and probe beside it is not: a registration that declares this one alone is refused, because leaving klass->start NULL with no probe of its own would send gst_device_provider_start into its unguarded klass->probe call (gstdeviceprovider.c:476-481). The dispatch of this one is guarded (gstdeviceprovider.c:522-536), so a provider that declares start alone, or probe alone, is fine. The bus is set flushing before the slot runs (gstdeviceprovider.c:532), so a DEVICE_REMOVED message posted by a DeviceRemove call from here reaches no listener - only the removed signal of the device fires - and the base class unparents every device that is still on the list once the slot returns (gstdeviceprovider.c:536-539). The slot runs with the start lock of the provider held (gstdeviceprovider.c:530-547): calling IsStarted, GetDevices, Start or Stop on the same provider from inside the override deadlocks on that non recursive mutex. DeviceAdd, DeviceRemove, DeviceChanged, HideProvider and GetBus are safe, because they take the object lock or no lock at all.
