vfuncDocNotes.GstAudio.AudioSrc::read: This runs on the thread of the ring buffer. Answer the number of bytes read into the block, and leave the timestamp at Gst.ClockTime.None unless the device gives one.
vfuncDocNotes.GstBase.PushSrc::create: Answering Ok without a buffer is not a way to produce nothing: the base class posts an element error on the bus for a NULL buffer, so a source with nothing to hand out answers a flow result that says so - Eos, Flushing or an error.

$comment-vfunc-non-null-returns: The slots whose caller dereferences the answer without checking it for NULL, with the value the trampoline answers when the managed override answered none. gst_base_transform_fixate_caps and gst_aggregator_default_update_src_caps both hand the answer straight to gst_caps_is_fixed / gst_pad_set_caps, and the aggregator has already consumed the input by then, so a NULL would be a crash or a lost buffer rather than a failed negotiation. The managed member therefore answers a non nullable type, and an override that answers null anyway is reported through the exception trap while the slot answers empty caps, on which negotiation fails cleanly. The four codec getcaps slots have that shape one level down: gstaudioencoder.c:1822-1824, gstaudiodecoder.c:2879-2881, gstvideodecoder.c:2143-2145 and gstvideoencoder.c:949-951 all answer the caps query with gst_query_set_caps_result followed by an unconditional gst_caps_unref, so a NULL answer would unref NULL and hand the peer a NULL result. The two editing services slots are there for a heavier reason: a NULL answer is a use-after-free in GES 1.28.6. ges-track-element.c:1022 references the nlesource while it is still floating, child_failure drops that reference again (1066-1070), the composition then sinks the one reference that is left and frees the object when the track element is removed, and ges_track_element_dispose unreferences it once more. The substitute is a floating identity element, which gst_bin_add sinks and owns (ges-source.c:205-208), so nothing feeds the substitute, the source produces no data and the pipeline cannot preroll, instead of the heap being corrupted.
$comment-vfunc-identity-buffers: The buffer a slot hands back may be the very one it was given, and the caller compares the two pointers: gst_base_src_get_range only unrefs the buffer it passed in when the slot answered a different one, and gst_base_transform_default_prepare_output_buffer explicitly allows *outbuf == inbuf for an in-place transform. A reference taken on an unchanged answer would therefore never be released, so the trampoline of a parameter listed here only mints one when the handle really changed.
$comment-vfunc-spans: The blocks a slot only reads, which the projection cannot tell from the ones it writes: the gir counts both by the parameter beside them and spells both as a gpointer, and a gpointer carries no constness. A block listed here becomes a ReadOnlySpan and every other one a Span. gst_audio_sink_ring_buffer_thread reads the samples out of the block it hands to write (gstaudiosink.c:247), while gst_audio_src_ring_buffer_thread expects read to fill the one it hands over (gstaudiosrc.c:223).
$comment-vfunc-floating-returns: The slots whose caller owns the floating reference of the answer. No gir transfer kind spells that - the annotation of such a slot is transfer none, which reads as a borrow - and the difference is a use-after-free rather than a nuance. gst_device_create_element hands the answer of its slot on exactly as it came (gstdevice.c:225) and raises a g_critical when it is not floating, which is what a wrapped answer always is because the wrapper sank the reference it holds when it was built (gstdevice.c:217-223, and the doc annotation at :201 says transfer floating). The caller is the owner from there on: gst-device-monitor.c:200,205 drops the answer with a bare gst_object_unref and never sinks it, while d3d11screencapturesrc.cpp:194 hands it to gst_bin_add_many, which does. A borrowed answer would leave the first caller unreferencing an object nobody handed it a reference of, and an owned one would leak the second reference on the path where the caller sinks; the trampoline of a listed slot therefore mints one reference and forces the floating flag back on, which touches no other reference count (gobject.c:4269-4276). What the override owes in return is in the generated documentation of the slot: answer a new, unparented instance on every call and keep no reference to it.
$comment-vfunc-sibling-arguments: The parameters that hand a slot a second instance of the type the slot itself runs for, which the base class has just created and still holds. Nothing in the gir says so - the parameter is an ordinary transfer-none GObject - and the difference is one of ownership: such an instance may still be floating, and settling that reference into a wrapper takes the one the caller means to drop. A parameter listed here is resolved the way the instance of the slot is, through TryGetOrFabricate, which interns or fabricates a wrapper and sinks nothing. GESTimelineElementClass::deep_copy is the one slot of the corpus with that shape. ges_timeline_element_copy extracts the copy from the asset of self, so it has the GType of self and is a fresh instance of the same managed subclass; GESTimelineElement derives from GInitiallyUnowned and nothing sinks the copy on the way, so it reaches the slot floating with a refcount of one. The floating reference is later dropped without ever being sunk: GESContainer::_deep_copy plain-stores the pointer (ges-container.c:332) and gst_object_unrefs it in _free_mapping (:129), and an application unrefs its own copy after pasting it. A wrapper that had sunk that reference would lose it to a free path that never knew about the wrapper.
$comment-lent-opaque-records: The opaque records a virtual method is lent one of. The wrapper of an opaque record is a bare pointer holder - the gir describes no way of releasing one - and the pointer a slot is lent is regularly an address on the stack of the caller: GstAudioRingBufferSpec is a field of the ring buffer the prepare slot is handed, and both GstVideoFrame arguments of the transform slots of a video filter are locals of gst_video_filter_transform_frame. The wrapper is therefore detached when the call returns, and every member of one that outlived the call throws ObjectDisposedException rather than reading an address that means nothing any more. The set is stated here rather than derived because a run plans and emits one module after the other: Gst.Meta is written out with the core module, and the slots that lend it - the transform_meta of the two audio codecs, of a base transform and of the two video codecs - belong to modules that are reached long afterwards. Both ways of the list going wrong are reported: a record a slot lends and this does not name is GEN0045, an error, and a record nothing lends is GEN0046.
$comment-vfunc-failure-values: What a trampoline answers when the exception trap caught an override, for the slots whose caller reads something other than a failure into the zero of the return type. The ring buffer thread of an audio sink calls write again with the same block when it answered zero and the ring buffer is started (gstaudiosink.c:257-259), and the one of an audio source loops on a read that answered zero as long as the source runs (gstaudiosrc.c:234); both treat a negative count as the error it is, which for the unsigned answer of read is the whole range of the type.
$comment-instance-keyed-callbacks: The eleven pad function typedefs carry no user_data parameter of their own: gstpad.c:4605 calls chainfunc (pad, parent, buffer), and the user_data the _full setter took stays on the pad in pad->chaindata and never reaches the handler. Each entry names the storage slot of the pad the setter writes, which is what the trampoline recovers the managed delegate by, together with the pad it is handed as its first argument. event and event_full share one slot because gst_pad_set_event_function_full and gst_pad_set_event_full_function_full write the same pad->eventdata and pad->eventnotify (gstpad.c:1933-1937, :1979-1984), so a pad carries one of the two and the later call frees the state of the earlier one.
$comment-doc-notes: Sentences the generated documentation of a member carries for a part of its contract that neither the gir nor the marshalling states, keyed by c:identifier. It is the counterpart of vfuncDocNotes for a member rather than for a class struct slot.

docNotes.ges_asset_needs_reload: The binding throws ArgumentException for a null id on a GESEffect, GESEffectClip, GESUriClip, GESAudioUriSource, GESVideoUriSource, GESMultiFileSource or GESTransitionClip type, and on GESSourceClip itself. docNotes.ges_timeline_element_list_children_prope: GES sorts the block by property name before it hands it back (ges-timeline-element.c:2260), so the array reads in ascending name order. Every specification carries a reference of its own: the default implementation references each one as it copies the registry of the element (ges-timeline-element.c:293-310) and the in-tree callers unreference every element and free the block (ges-track-element.c:1649-1652), which is what the wrappers do here. An element that registered no child property answers an empty array rather than nothing (ges-timeline-element.c:2255-2256).
docNotes.ges_track_element_get_all_control_bindin: The dictionary is a snapshot of the table the element keeps (ges-track-element.c:1253-1274), so a binding added or removed afterwards does not change it. Every key is the child property name exactly as it was given to SetControlSource, which GES stores without normalising it (ges-track-element.c:1961-1969): the plain form, alpha, and the qualified one, GstFramePositioner::alpha, can both appear in one table (the positioner is the child a GES video source resolves alpha to; ges/gstframepositioner.c:614). The bindings belong to the objects they were installed on and the wrappers are interned, so they are the very instances GetControlBinding answers and must not be disposed. An element that carries no binding answers an empty dictionary rather than nothing, because the table is created in the instance initializer (ges-track-element.c:515-516).
docNotes.gst_allocator_register: The registry keeps the reference the call is handed for good: gstallocator.c:237 flags the allocator MAY_BE_LEAKED before the insert, which is the C stating that the reference is never released, and no member takes an allocator out of the registry again. Registering the same name a second time is the one thing that releases one: the table was built with gst_object_unref as the destructor of its values (gstallocator.c:611-612), so the insert at :238-239 drops the reference the previous registration was handed, never the one this call is handed. The wrapper is the caller's either way, and Find answers with it for as long as it lives.

docNotes.gst_debug_get_all_categories: The list is a snapshot of the category registry taken under the lock that guards it (gstinfo.c:2663-2682 copies the spine of the static list), so a category registered afterwards is not in it and a second call may answer a longer list. The categories themselves belong to the library: one is kept per name (gstinfo.c:2513-2546 dedups under the same lock and frees the loser), none is reference counted, and they are released in one sweep by gst_deinit and nowhere else, so the wrappers here are borrowed handles that must never be disposed and the deliberately empty gst_debug_category_free is not to be called on one either. Only the spine is the caller's, which this frees. The list is never empty after gst_init, which creates the default category among others (gstinfo.c:613-678); a build with the debug system compiled out is the one that answers nothing.
docNotes.gst_mikey_message_get_cs_srtp: The structure is copied out of the GArray the message keeps its crypto session map in (gstmikey.c:1004-1014 answers the address of the element at the index), so it is a snapshot of the entry as it stood at the call and nothing of it points back into the message. The entry itself is valid until the map of the message is changed - inserting, removing or replacing a session (gstmikey.c:1030-1045, :1059-1070, :1082-1093) may move every later entry - or until the message is freed, so an index read again after a change may name a different entry. An index past the last entry answers nothing; a message whose map type is not SRTP raises a critical and answers nothing as well.
docNotes.gst_mikey_payload_sp_get_param: The structure is copied out of the GArray the payload keeps its security policy parameters in (gstmikey.c:489-499 answers the address of the element at the index), but the value bytes are not: ValPtr addresses the block the payload owns (gstmikey.c:539-557 duplicates the bytes into it) and Val reads them from there at the time it is asked. The parameter, and the bytes with it, are valid until the parameters of the payload are changed - adding a parameter may move every later entry and removing one frees its bytes (gstmikey.c:508-524) - or until the payload or the message that carries it is freed. An index past the last parameter answers nothing; a payload that is not a security policy payload raises a critical and answers nothing as well.

docNotes.gst_rtsp_mount_points_add_factory: A path that does not begin with '/' is refused with an ArgumentException before the call: rtsp-mount-points.c:354 answers such a path with a g_return_if_fail before it takes the factory, and the reference minted for the call would then have no owner. The mount keeps the reference the call is handed until the path is unmounted with RemoveFactory, replaced by another factory at the same path, or the mount points are finalised: the C stores the pointer in a bare field of the mount item (rtsp-mount-points.c:358) and releases it once in data_item_free (:71). The wrapper is the caller's and stays usable, which matters here more than anywhere else in the module: a media factory is the hook point of a server, and disposing the wrapper runs DisconnectAll, which takes the MediaConfigure and MediaConstructed handlers off again while the mount keeps serving. Keep the wrapper for as long as the mount is expected to call back into managed code.
docNotes.gst_uri_get_media_fragment_table: The table is parsed afresh on every call out of the fragment of the URI and is kept nowhere (gsturi.c:2979-3008): the fragment is split at every & and each part at its first =, and both halves are percent decoded, so the last of two entries with the same key wins. The dictionary is therefore a value of its own, and editing it does not touch the URI. A key that carries no = has a null value and one written as key= has an empty one. A URI without a fragment answers nothing, while one whose fragment is empty answers an empty dictionary. The order of the entries is the iteration order of the table GLib built and is not specified.
docNotes.gst_uri_get_query_table: The dictionary is a snapshot. C hands out the live query table of the URI (gsturi.c:2733-2759) and this copies it, so editing the dictionary does not change the URI: SetQueryTable is what writes a whole table back. A key that stands in the query without an = has a null value and one written as key= has an empty one, which is the difference the query string keeps. A URI without a query answers nothing, while one whose query is empty answers an empty dictionary. The order of the entries is the iteration order of the table GLib built and is not specified.
docNotes.gst_uri_set_query_table: The entries are copied into a table of its own that the URI keeps and goes on editing (gsturi.c:2761-2797), so the dictionary may be changed or dropped afterwards without affecting the URI. A null dictionary takes the query out of the URI, while an empty one gives it a query with no keys at all. A null value produces a key that stands in the query string with no = after it. The values are typed string? because of that key, and IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue> is invariant in TValue, so a Dictionary<string, string> does not convert to one: declare the dictionary as Dictionary<string, string?>, or write ! at the call site, which is sound because the call only reads what it is given. The call answers false, after a GLib critical, when the URI is not writable, which is what a URI that is shared is.
docNotes.gst_webrtc_ice_add_candidate: The promise is not answered on every path, and on the older releases it is answered on no successful one. At 1.24.13 and 1.26.11 the libnice implementation replies only where it refuses the candidate - an address it cannot parse (nice.c:868), an address that is not .local (nice.c:885), and the two failures of the asynchronous .local resolve (nice.c:782, :819) - while the end-of-candidates call (nice.c:846-849), a candidate libnice accepts (nice.c:915) and a .local address that does resolve (nice.c:828-829) leave it pending for good, so a caller that waits on it there waits forever. Nothing interrupts or expires it either. 1.28.0 added the reply on the two synchronous success paths (302c2dc5dc, not backported: 1.28.6 nice.c:882 for end-of-candidates and :953 for an accepted candidate), and even 1.28.6 does not reply when a .local candidate resolves successfully (nice.c:861-862). Nothing is leaked on any of them: the synchronous paths neither reference nor release the promise, and the asynchronous one holds a reference of its own (nice.c:899 at 1.24.13) that its destroy notify drops (nice.c:741). Pass null unless the host is 1.28 or newer and the candidate is one of the two paths that answer there.
docNotes.gst_webrtc_ice_find_transport: The base function is a pure vfunc dispatch: it checks the instance, asserts the slot and hands the answer of the implementation back unchanged (ice.c:79-97, byte-identical at 1.24.13, 1.26.11 and 1.28.6), so what the ownership of the answer is, is decided by the implementation below it - libnice's, which is the only one the binding meets. There a transport that the stream already listed comes back with a reference of its own, while a fresh one came back floating with only a weak reference behind it until gst_object_ref_sink (ret) was added (nicestream.c:193-200 at 1.28.6, absent at nicestream.c:193-199 of 1.24.13; commit 83b8417290 with the 1.26 backport 9e7a2e6363, first tags 1.26.11 and 1.28.1). The wrapper sinks a floating handle and takes no further reference, which is one owner on every release of either shape: the sink converts the floating reference rather than adding one, and a transport that was already sunk is adopted as it is. Dispose what comes back exactly once.
docNotes.gst_webrtc_ice_stream_find_transport: A transport the stream already listed comes back with a reference of its own, taken by the g_weak_ref_get of the walk (nicestream.c:179-184 at 1.24.13). A fresh one is built with gst_webrtc_nice_transport_new, which is a bare g_object_new on a GstObject (nicetransport.c:421-424 at 1.24.13), and the list the stream keeps holds nothing but a weak reference to it, so before gst_object_ref_sink (ret) was added at nicestream.c:196 it came back floating - commit 83b8417290, backported to 1.26 as 9e7a2e6363, first tags 1.26.11 and 1.28.1, so 1.24.x, 1.26.0 through 1.26.10 and 1.28.0 hand out the floating one. Either shape is one owner here: the wrapper sinks a floating handle, which converts that reference rather than adding one, and takes no further reference otherwise. Dispose what comes back exactly once, on every release.

$comment-preconditions: C# statements the generated body of a callable runs before it marshals anything, keyed by c:identifier. They are written out verbatim, in this order, after the argument null checks and before the first stackalloc, scope or handle read, so that a statement may read the parameter it refuses and a statement that throws finds nothing allocated. The generator validates nothing about them: the helper each one calls is hand written in the Custom/ partial of the type that carries the member, so the C# compiler reports one that names nothing, and GEN0049 reports a key no rendered callable consumed. The entries below are of four kinds. The ges_ ones refuse what GES dereferences without a guard: an effect with no asset, whose bin description the top effect branch reads through ges_asset_get_id (NULL) (ges-clip.c:1786-1790), and a null asset id, which the check_id of an effect type splits and reads a token out of (ges-effect-asset.c:390-391). The buffer ones refuse a buffer that is not writable, because gst_buffer_add_meta answers NULL for a shared buffer (gstbuffer.c:2326-2376, :2335) and these adders use that answer without checking it. The gst_bus_ ones refuse a bus built without asynchronous delivery, because the members below reach for a GstPoll that such a bus never built and the C answers nothing a caller could act on (gstbus.c:550, :889-910, :1217-1219). The gst_rtsp_ one refuses a mount point path that does not begin with '/', because C turns such a call away without taking the factory, leaving the reference minted for it with no owner (rtsp-mount-points.c:354). The keys are in ordinal order.

$comment-hand-over-refusals: Callables that refuse what they are handed before they take it, keyed by c:identifier, with the citation of the C lines the reading rests on as the value. The generated body releases the reference minted for every handed over argument again right after the call when the call refused it, which the raw result spells as a zero: FALSE for a gboolean return and NULL for a pointer one. The entry is the statement that the refusal return means the reference was not taken, which only the C can settle: a callable whose C releases the reference itself on refusal - ges_project_save, gst_rtsp_server_transfer_connection - must not be listed, because the release would be the second one. The return contract of the member is unchanged. GEN0050 reports an entry on a callable that answers neither a gboolean nor a pointer, or that hands no argument over, and GEN0051 reports a key no rendered callable read.

$comment-doc-strip: Substrings taken out of the gir documentation of a callable before it is split into paragraphs, keyed by c:identifier. It is the one overlay that removes upstream text instead of adding to it, and it exists for the sentence that states a rule of the C which is not the rule of the binding: a transfer-full GObject argument is handed a reference minted for the call, so the wrapper stays usable and 'should not be used after calling this function' is true of a C caller only. Each substring has to stand in the raw documentation exactly once - it is quoted from girs/reference/*.gir, gtk-doc markup and line breaks included - and GEN0052 reports one that stands nowhere or twice, so an upstream rewording is reported rather than silently stripping nothing. GEN0053 reports a key no rendered callable read. Once an entry has taken something out, the whitespace of that member's whole documentation is tidied rather than only the seam: inside every line a run of spaces that follows text collapses to one and trailing spaces go, and two blank lines in a row become the one paragraph break the removal left behind. The indentation a line opens with is kept, because that is the shape of a fenced sample. A member no entry changed is not normalised at all.

$comment-type-doc-replace: Substrings of the gir documentation of a CLASS and the text written in their place, keyed by qualified gir name with an old/new pair per replacement. It is the replacing counterpart of docStrip, one level up: for the upstream sentence that documents a string grammar the library itself does not write that way, where a removal would take the example away and a note beside it would leave the reader two grammars and no way to choose. Replacements are applied in the order they are written, each to the text the one before left behind, and every failure is GEN0064 and an error - an old standing nowhere or more than once, a class with no documentation at all, a key no rendered class read - so a gir refresh that corrects the sentence upstream stops the run instead of leaving the entry to rot. Only classes are covered, including the holder of a fundamental; records and interfaces obtain their type documentation on emitter paths of their own.
